description: We are a duo of Information Systems students building an interactive web-based decision support tool for the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge. By leveraging NASA climate and soil moisture datasets, our platform visualizes local agricultural conditions and recommends optimal crop rotations to improve soil health. Our core focus is on Agriculture, Web Development, and Data Visualization!
summary: TaniShift is a web-based agroclimatological Decision Support System (DSS) developed to help smallholder farmers and agricultural extension workers in West Java plan sustainable, cross-family crop rotations and restore post-harvest soil fertility. Addressing the Field Shift challenge, TaniShift integrates a three-year (2023–2025) satellite climate baseline from NASA POWER, combining root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT from SMAP/MERRA-2), bias-corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR from GPM), and 2-meter surface temperature (T2M) on a 0.5° grid, with local soil taxonomy (Latosol, Inceptisol, and volcanic Andosol). Without requiring expensive in-field sensors, the platform translates NASA Earth observation data into an interactive 12-month planting calendar, soil nutrient diagnostics, and 24 curated rotation recommendations across six botanical families for Sumedang Selatan, Tanjungsari, and Pangalengan. This solution is vital because continuous monoculture depletes soil nutrients, compacts hardpan layers, and accelerates soil-borne pathogens, while shifting weather disrupts traditional farming schedules. By democratizing NASA open space data, TaniShift enables biological soil recovery, reduces chemical dependency, and strengthens climate-resilient food production.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

TaniShift (Field Shift Decision Support System) is a zero-setup precision agroclimatology web platform designed to help smallholder farmers and agricultural extension workers in West Java, Indonesia, plan cross-family crop rotations and restore post-harvest soil fertility without costly physical IoT sensors in the field.

Built on a 3-year (2023–2025) climate data record from NASA POWER at 0.5° spatial grid resolution, TaniShift evaluates three core MERRA-2 reanalysis parameters—Root-Zone Soil Wetness (GWETROOT), Observation-Corrected Daily Rainfall (PRECTOTCORR), and Surface Air Temperature at 2 meters (T2M)—across three distinct agricultural case-study regions: Sumedang Selatan (-6.86°, 107.92°), Tanjungsari (-6.91°, 107.79°), and Pangalengan (-7.18°, 107.57°).

Users follow an intuitive 3-step workflow:

1. Select a farming region via dropdown or an interactive SVG 0.5° satellite grid map.

2. Select one of four recently harvested starter crops: Rice, Maize (Poaceae), Chili, or Potato (Solanaceae).

3. Instantly receive a soil-residue diagnosis (identifying N, P, K, and Si deficits, plow-pan/hardpan compaction, and soil-borne pathogens like Ralstonia solanacearum and Phytophthora), a clickable 12-month planting window calendar categorizing Dry (< 3.5 mm/day), Ideal Rotation Window (3.5–7.5 mm/day), and Wet (> 7.5 mm/day) phases, two cross-family replacement crop recommendations from a curated 24-scenario matrix across 6 botanical families (with match scores from 86% to 96%), local pedology profiles (Latosol, Inceptisol, and Volcanic Andosol), and multi-year Chart.js moisture-rainfall trend charts.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

- Biological Soil Fertility Restoration: Alternating nutrient-depleting monocultures (Poaceae/Solanaceae) with nitrogen-fixing legumes (e.g., Soybean adding +45–60 kg N/ha naturally) breaks soil-borne pest and pathogen cycles, loosens compacted hardpan layers, and reduces dependence on synthetic fertilizers and chemical pesticides.

- Evidence-Based Crop Failure Risk Mitigation: Translating 3-year satellite rainfall and root-moisture records into a clear monthly planting window helps farmers avoid vegetative-phase drought or early-season root rot caused by shifting rainy and dry seasons.

- Scalable & Sensor-Free Accessibility: Runs directly in desktop and mobile browsers without hardware installation or expensive servers, making it immediately ready to scale to other agricultural grid coordinates across Indonesia.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

- Frontend & Architecture: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and modular Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+ separated into app.js, sumedang.js, tanjungsari.js, and pangalengan.js).

- Data Visualization & Mapping: Chart.js for multi-year combined bar-line agroclimatology charts and custom interactive SVG 0.5° coordinate mapping.

- Data & Deployment: NASA POWER Data Access Viewer / API (2023–2025 CSV time-series datasets), Visual Studio Code, Git, and GitHub Pages (Live Demo: https://firdausysalsa.github.io/tanishift-project/).

Creativity & Factors Considered:

Rather than showing raw satellite numbers that are difficult for farmers to interpret, TaniShift creatively bridges space-borne Earth observation data (NASA POWER / MERRA-2) with local soil taxonomy (soil orders, pH, organic carbon) and botanical family rotation rules (explicitly preventing same-family replanting). Our team specifically accounted for smallholder accessibility (zero hardware cost, mobile browser compatibility), local West Java micro-climates ranging from mid-elevation irrigated paddies to highland horticulture, and practical field guidance such as exact dolomite lime (0.5–1.5 tons/ha) and rice-straw mulch applications.
